text.p: Den Danske Bank, Denmark's biggest bank, was a more efficient earner in 1996 than its rival Unidanmark, an analysis showed on Thursday.
The banks' 1996 annual reports, issued this week, showed Den Danske's cost-income ratio last year at 1.71 times compared to Unidanmark's 1.44 times.
The comparative figures for 1995 were 1.64 for Den Danske and 1.50 for Unidanmark, the banks' calculations showed.
Figures for 1996 core earnings showed a similar picture with Den Danske's rising 34 percent to 3.730 billion crowns against Unidanmark's meagre five percent rise to 1.912 billion crowns.
Earlier on Thursday Den Danske Bank announced 1996 profits before tax and ordinary items of 5.396 billion crowns, compared to 1995's 6.034 billion crowns.
On Wednesday Unidanmark posted a 2.801 billion crown profit for the same item against a 2.969 billion crowns surplus in 1995.
Den Danske predicted little growth in core earnings this year, while Unidanmark said it aimed to reduce its cost-income ratio "on an ongoing basis."
